title: SwiftUI Rules
tagline: Small views, minimal state, logic outside the View, styles from the design system, text via keys, meaningful names.
intro: Small views, minimal state, logic outside the View, styles from the design system, text via keys, meaningful names.

blocks.html:
1. Small views, one job each. If body exceeds ~50 lines, extract subviews.
  2. body only describes UI. No heavy computation, no network calls, no business logic.
  3. Extract subviews as struct, not computed properties, when the view has state or is reusable.
  4. No AnyView. Use @ViewBuilder or generics.
  5. Conditional modifiers take a parameter. Avoid wrapping modifiers in if (it changes the view type and loses state/animation).
    • Write alerts in the full, labeled form. Put each argument on its own line; use actions: and message: closures instead of trailing-closure shorthand. Inside an alert, use Button(_:role:action:) and write the action closure explicitly. The title is the first unlabeled argument because SwiftUI's API declares it with _.
      swift
      .alert(
    "project.delete.title", // titleKey (the API uses an unlabeled argument)
    isPresented: $isDeleteAlertShown, // Binding<Bool>
    actions: { // Returns the alert buttons
        Button(
            "project.delete.confirm",
            role: .destructive,
            action: {
                viewModel.delete()
            }
        )
        Button(
            "common.cancel",
            role: .cancel,
            action: {} // The alert closes automatically
        )
    },
    message: { // Returns the supporting message
        Text("project.delete.message")
    }
)

blocks.html:
1. Use the right property wrapper, and keep state as low as possible:
    • @State: view-local state (should be private)
    • @Binding: child edits the parent's state
    • @Observable (iOS 17+) / @StateObject: view model
    • @Environment: shared dependencies
  2. Single source of truth. Never copy state into two places.
  3. Use an enum for status instead of multiple loose Bools (idle / loading / loaded / failed).

blocks.html:
1. Views know nothing about network or database. They only talk to the ViewModel.
  2. Dependencies come in through init or a DI container. Never call singletons directly inside a View. Name stored dependency properties and local parameter variables with their role suffix: ...UseCase, ...Repository, or ...DataSource. For example, use loadSettingsUseCase, accessRepository, and accessLocalDataSource. Preserve an existing public argument label when compatibility requires it: init(repository accessRepository: any AccessRepository) keeps the repository: call label while naming the local variable accessRepository.
  3. Organize modules by feature. Each feature owns its View + ViewModel + UseCase.
  4. Keep logic out of the View so it is testable (the ViewModel should not import SwiftUI if possible).

blocks.html:
1. Every UI uses shared DesignSystem tokens: DSColor for every color, DSSpacing for spacing, dimensions, and corner radii, and DSTextStyle for text. Do not write Color.*, numeric spacing, or .font(...) directly in a View; add a named token when a needed value is missing.

    • DSSpacing is an enum namespace for spacing, corner radii, and control sizes. Names use the numeric value, such as spacing8 for 8 points and spacing50 for a 50-point button height. For example, VStack(spacing: DSSpacing.spacing8) { ... } puts 8 points between its children.

    • DSTextStyle lives in the DesignSystem package and provides fixed styles as .modifier(DSTextStyle.body). RootView applies body as the default for the whole app; apply a more specific style to text that needs one. Each style sets font family, point size, weight, and line-height target. The sans family is system SF Pro; the monospaced family is SF Mono.

      StyleFamilySizeWeightLine height
      largeTitleSF Pro34 ptBold41 pt
      titleSF Pro24 ptBold30 pt
      pageTitleSF Pro28 ptBold34 pt
      sectionSF Pro20 ptSemibold25 pt
      headlineSF Pro17 ptSemibold22 pt
      bodySF Pro17 ptRegular22 pt
      subheadSF Pro15 ptRegular20 pt
      footnoteSF Pro13 ptRegular18 pt
      captionSF Pro10 ptMedium12 pt
      codeSF Mono13 ptRegular18 pt
      figureSF Pro28 ptSemibold34 pt

      SwiftUI exposes line spacing rather than an exact line-height property. The modifier applies the token's extra leading as lineSpacing; single-line text keeps the same font metrics.

    • Use the closest existing token. Add a token only when the design needs a genuinely new value, and keep its value in the shared type so screens do not each define their own.

  2. Repeated styling becomes a ViewModifier / ButtonStyle.
  3. Every view has a #Preview with sample data.

blocks.html:
1. Use keys for translatable UI copy; keep fixed values out of the catalog. Put names, dates, IDs, counts, measurements, and file names directly in Presentation.
    swift
    Text("access.sign_in.title")                    // ✅ UI copy key
Text(verbatim: "Riverside Tower B")             // ✅ fixed value
Text("Seed data")                               // ❌ hard-coded UI copy
String(localized: "access.sign_in.description") // ✅ when a String is needed
  2. Name keys by UI role, not by the displayed wording. Use short snake_case segments, such as access.sign_in.title, access.sign_in.description, or access.sign_in.benefit_1. Store the real copy in the String Catalog.
  3. No string concatenation. Use placeholders and plurals in the String Catalog (Localizable.xcstrings).
    swift
    Text("devmenu.finished \(name)")            // ✅ placeholder
Text(name + " finished")                    // ❌ concatenation
  4. Models and ViewModels return keys (LocalizedStringResource or LocalizedStringKey), not already-translated strings. Note: Text(someString) with a String variable is not localized. Only Text("literal") or Text(LocalizedStringKey) is.

blocks.html:
1. UI runs on @MainActor. Use async/await for heavy work, no nested callbacks.
  2. Use .task { } instead of onAppear { Task { } } (it cancels automatically when the view disappears).

blocks.html:
1. Name things by meaning: isLoading, didTapSave(). Never flag1, handle().
  2. Use SwiftLint + SwiftFormat in CI so the whole team shares one style.
  3. Support Dark Mode and Accessibility (accessibilityLabel) from day one. Use DSTextStyle for every UI text style; do not use SwiftUI's default font or a local .font(...) override.

blocks.html:
swift
enum DevAction: CaseIterable, Identifiable {
    case seedData
    case deleteAllData
    case resetApp

    var id: Self { self }

    var title: LocalizedStringKey {
        switch self {
        case .seedData: "devmenu.seed.title"
        case .deleteAllData: "devmenu.deleteAll.title"
        case .resetApp: "devmenu.reset.title"
        }
    }

    var subtitle: LocalizedStringKey {
        switch self {
        case .seedData: "devmenu.seed.subtitle"
        case .deleteAllData: "devmenu.deleteAll.subtitle"
        case .resetApp: "devmenu.reset.subtitle"
        }
    }
}

Developer log strings (AppLogger) do not need localization. Add a separate var logName: String for logging if needed.

• body is short, with no business logic
  • State uses the right wrapper, with no duplicated source
  • Status uses an enum, not multiple Bools
  • Views do not call network/database/singletons directly
  • No hard-coded colors, fonts, or spacing
  • UI colors, spacing, dimensions, radii, and text use DSColor, DSSpacing, and DSTextStyle
  • No hard-coded UI strings, keys are used
  • #Preview is present
  • Accessibility labels exist for important icons/buttons
